result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): The two answers are very close. Both explain the scan's limits, identify the div time slots as the blocker, fix them with radio buttons in a fieldset that show 'fully booked' in text, and add a role=status confirmation. B edges ahead because it says outright that removing the aria-labels lets speech and screen-reader users hear the visible words. Its code is also more complete: it includes CSS that hides the radios but keeps them focusable, moves focus to the time field when no time is chosen, and gives a readable confirmation instead of '19:00'. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): The two answers are close: both correctly diagnose the div time slots, the hidden names that differ from the visible text, and the success shown only by a green border, and both offer nearly the same fix using native radio buttons and a live region. A edges ahead because it says the name mismatch affects both speech-control and screen-reader users, moves focus to the field on each validation error, and writes a readable confirmation ('6:00 pm' instead of '18:00'). B has a cleaner native form submit and a useful warning against display:none, but it doesn't say how the name mismatch affects screen-reader users and doesn't move focus when no time is chosen.
